questions.scenario: Caribbean Disaster Management Centre is upgrading its computer and communications systems. Several branches will share information with a central system and staff will access some services remotely.

visual.caption: Caribbean Disaster Management Centre proposed network

parts.prompt: State TWO characteristics of a supercomputer that make it suitable for weather and disaster modelling.
markScheme: Award 1 mark for each relevant characteristic linked to the workload, for example high processing capacity, ability to handle many transactions/users, specialised control, reliability or large data volumes.

parts.prompt: Identify the MOST important hardware device used to connect the local networks to other networks.
markScheme: Router. 1 mark.
Role/function correctly stated as connecting or forwarding data between networks. 1 mark.

parts.prompt: Distinguish between an intranet and an extranet.
markScheme: Intranet is private/internal to an organisation. 1 mark.
Extranet gives controlled access to authorised external users. 1 mark.
Clear distinction or suitable example. 1 mark.

parts.prompt: State THREE transmission media that could be used in computer networks.
markScheme: Any three suitable media, for example twisted pair, coaxial cable, fibre-optic cable, infrared, microwave or satellite. 1 mark each.

parts.prompt: State TWO factors, other than cost, that should be considered when deciding whether to store operational files in the cloud.
markScheme: Any two relevant factors such as accessibility, security, capacity, Internet availability/reliability or organisational policy. 1 mark each.

parts.prompt: Explain why verification and validation are BOTH useful when new records are entered.
markScheme: Validation checks whether data follows specified rules. 1 mark.
Verification checks whether data was entered/copied accurately. 1 mark.
Explanation that both address different kinds of data-entry error. 1 mark.

parts.prompt: The organisation receives an email asking staff to follow a link and enter their passwords urgently. Identify the likely threat and state TWO precautions staff should take.
markScheme: Phishing/social-engineering attempt. 1 mark.

Any two suitable precautions such as verify sender/domain, do not follow suspicious link, type official address manually, do not reveal credentials, report the message. Up to 4 marks for two well-stated precautions.

questions.scenario: Caribbean Disaster Management Centre needs a small program to calculate a evacuation score and make a simple decision. The program must be designed before it is implemented.

Calculate SCORE using all three values. 2 marks.
Correct IF condition using threshold. 1 mark.
Display ACCEPT on true branch. 1 mark.
ELSE/otherwise branch. 1 mark.

parts.prompt: Explain how a trace table or dry run could be used to test the algorithm.
markScheme: Use selected test data. 1 mark.
Record changing values/identifiers step by step. 1 mark.
Follow decision/control flow. 1 mark.

parts.prompt: Distinguish between a syntax error and a logic error.
markScheme: Syntax error breaks language rules and may prevent successful translation/execution. 1–2 marks.

parts.prompt: State THREE features of good internal program documentation.
